 Mavericks vs. Thunder game preview
 Wednesday brings an unbeaten Oklahoma City team to American Airlines Center, but Mark Daigneault's rotation has taken several hits. Jalen Williams fractured his left fibula and dislocated his left ankle against the Clippers, while Cason Wallace tore his shoulder labrum. Both need surgery. Chet Holmgren has also been sidelined by a knee issue, and Alex Caruso sprained his ankle Monday against Phoenix. The Thunder still won 125-114, as Ajay Mitchell scored a career-high 30 and Shai Gilgeous-Alexander added 26.
 Dallas comes home after a 113-109 victory at Miami. Cooper Flagg scored 29 points and distributed 11 assists, then blocked a potential go-ahead shot in the final minute. P.J. Washington added 20 points, and Kyrie Irving scored 18. The Mavericks have split their first four games under Dusty May. Flagg had 12 fourth-quarter points against the Heat and finished with five steals. Walter Clayton Jr. contributed 15 points off the bench. Dallas also lost to Houston by 18 and San Antonio by 16, leaving both defeats outside Wednesday's selected margin.
 Oklahoma City has won its four games by seven to 12 points, holding Denver to 84 in its second outing. Gilgeous-Alexander scored 34 against the Clippers in Sunday's 108-101 victory. Monday's 125-114 victory over Phoenix finally pushed the Thunder past this figure. Mitchell's 30 points were particularly valuable with multiple regulars unavailable, while Isaiah Hartenstein supplied 15 points and 13 rebounds.
